transcript.text: First inspect files. for f in ['chart.py','summary.txt','table.csv']: print('=== ',f); print(open(f).read()) continue

table.csv has Youth_Unemployment_Rate starting at 15.2 and Informal_Employment_Rate starting at 78.5, but chart.py has those two lists the other way round. That is flaw (1), the swapped series. Flaw (2) is the y-axis label: it reads 'Country', but the axis plots the rate in percent. The fix swaps the data lists so each column gets its own values, keeping the series order and therefore the colours (youth red, informal golden-yellow). It also sets the y label to 'Rate (%)'. I then check the result against table.csv. src = open('chart.py').read() import re y_start = src.index("'Youth_Unemployment_Rate': [") i_start = src.index("'Informal_Employment_Rate': [") y_end = src.index("]", y_start)+1 i_end = src.index("]", i_start)+1 y_block = src[y_start:y_end]; i_block = src[i_start:i_end] y_vals = y_block[y_block.index('['):]; i_vals = i_block[i_block.index('['):] new = src[:y_start] + "'Youth_Unemployment_Rate': " + i_vals + src[y_end:i_start] + "'Informal_Employment_Rate': " + y_vals + src[i_end:] new = new.replace("plt.ylabel('Country', fontsize=12)", "plt.ylabel('Rate (%)', fontsize=12)") with open('chart.py','w') as f: f.write(new) exec(compile(new,'chart.py','exec')) import pandas as pd t = pd.read_csv('table.csv') m = df.merge(t, on='Country', suffixes=('','_t')) print(len(m), (m.Youth_Unemployment_Rate==m.Youth_Unemployment_Rate_t).all(), (m.Informal_Employment_Rate==m.Informal_Employment_Rate_t).all()) ax = plt.gca(); print(ax.get_ylabel(), ax.get_ylim(), ax.get_legend_handles_labels()[1]) continue
